messages:
nora: Heads-up — in eu-west2 we've got ~40 Pending GPU pods even though autoscaler spun up nodes. It's weird: nodes show Available but scheduler keeps saying 'no fit' for those pods.

sam: Can you paste the pod describe? maybe it's a resource request mismatch or nodeSelector.

nora: Here's a failing pod describe (trimmed):
```
Events:
  2m   Warning  FailedScheduling  pod/myjob-5  0/28 nodes are available: 12 Insufficient gpu, 16 node(s) didn't match node selector.
  1m   Normal   NotTriggerScaleUp  pod/myjob-5  pod fits existing nodes, but cluster autoscaler can't increase GPU nodes in this AZ.
```
Node labels we use: `gpu-type=nvidia-a100`, `zone=eu-west2-b`, `spot=true|false`.

priya: NotTriggerScaleUp message is interesting — cluster-autoscaler thinks placement could work if nodes were added but we hit regional quota or quota per AZ? Did cloud console show quota limits? Also check `kube-scheduler` logs around 14:10.

ops-bot: [autoscaler] scaleUp: requested 3 nodes from pool gpu-eu-west2-b-preemptible (reason: 12 pending pods). QuotaRemaining: 0 in eu-west2-b. (autoscaler v1.28.0)

nora: Confirmed — AZ quota for GPUs is exhausted in eu-west2-b. But we still have empty GPUs on nodes in eu-west2-c, and pods have a zone affinity via `nodeSelector: zone: eu-west2-b` because of local NVMe-backed dataset.

chris: That explains it — binpacking issue compounded by AZ-scoped quotas + strict nodeSelector. We're fragmenting GPUs across AZs. Two quick options: 1) relax strict `zone` selector for non-latency jobs, or 2) introduce a cross-AZ fallback pool (with data pulled from object storage) and update topology constraints.

sam: Also saw kube-proxy conntrack saturation in the same cluster earlier today. Some kubelets were flapping under load which delayed readiness and made CA think nodes weren't available when pods were considered for binpack. Logs:
```
Jun 3 14:08 kubelet[...]: E0900 kubelet: failed to update node status: conntrack table full
```
That increases scheduling churn.

priya: Agree. Two different causes stacking: AZ quota + networking/conntrack -> scheduler sees less usable capacity. The fragmentation metric from our binpacking dashboard shows ~22% of GPU memory idle across the fleet while 35 pods are pending.

nora: Cost angle — we're paying for preemptible GPU nodes in 3 AZs but can't place pods due to selectors and quotas. So utilization drops while bills remain high.

chris: Proposed immediate mitigations:
- Add an autoscaler override to permit bursting into eu-west2-c for this workload (requires quota request) OR
- Create a `gpu-fallback` nodepool in eu-west2-c with `data-cache: s3-backed` and relax zone selector on jobs that can tolerate remote data.
- Short-term: reduce conntrack pressure by lowering `maxPerCore` and enabling conntrack helpers offload.

sam: What about packing strategy? Could we use a tighter pod-level `requests` vs `limits` policy so smaller inference jobs pack 2-3 per GPU instead of 1? Maybe set `requests.gpu: 0.25` via device plugin fractional support or use muxing container.

priya: Fractional GPUs are risky for some models (OOMs). But for small batches we can run a lightweight muxer that time-shares the GPU at the driver level. That needs a new nodepool profile though.

nora: Short action items:
1) Priya: file quota increase request for eu-west2-b GPUs and link the ticket here. (start: now)
2) Sam: triage kube-proxy/conntrack config, roll a kube-proxy change to reduce conntrack by today EOD. (start: 30m)
3) Chris: prototype `gpu-fallback` nodepool in eu-west2-c with `data-cache` and `tolerations` to accept relaxed jobs. (start: tomorrow)
4) Nora: update job helm charts to allow zone fallback for non-local-data jobs. (start: tomorrow)

chris: I'll also run a quick cost calc: if we reclaim 20% GPU idle we save ~€7k/month for this cluster. I'll post numbers in #finance after prototyping.

priya: tagging in @infra on the quota ticket, and I'll schedule a short postmortem if repo rate doesn't drop after the fixes. :spiral_calendar:

sam: +1. if anyone sees more `NotTriggerScaleUp` events, paste autoscaler logs; that message is the key to whether it's quota or CA heuristics.

nora: thanks all — will post updates here as each item progresses. :thumbsup:
